method: Static control-flow and data-flow review using dnfile/dncil CIL disassembly, manual PowerShell/JScript deobfuscation, isolated evaluation of the pure JavaScript string decoder, resource extraction, osslsigncode, atomscan and cleave facts. No sample program or payload was executed. RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md read first. Reputation supplied by the user was treated as a lead.

samples.identification: CV-lure HTA remote-code loader delivering an XWorm-branded RAT from the live endpoint
samples.reason: Automatic concealed privileged HTTP-response evaluation and the recovered hidden PowerShell/DLL/RAT chain outweigh a hypothetical legitimate document use. No authorization or benign deployment context was supplied. Static malicious behavior is established independently of reputation and runtime success.
trace: UTF-16LE HTA starts with a builder placeholder %codigo_js%, declares no taskbar entry and minimized/chromeless controls, calls window.resizeTo(0,0) and window.moveTo(-2000,-2000), then invokes RunPayload from window.onload.

RunPayload constructs MSXML2.ServerXMLHTTP.6.0, synchronously GETs https://imperiailmports.com/yCkifY0p, assigns baselining.responseText to flybane and calls eval(flybane). Errors are swallowed and the HTA closes. No user-facing CV content exists.

Forager recovered the live referenced JScript on 2026-10-22. Removing inert huge numeric arrays exposes a WScript.Shell/FileSystemObject stager. It removes the repeated labichoreic token, writes a randomly named temporary .ps1, constructs hidden/policy-bypass PowerShell, then launches it using Win32_Process via SWbemLocator with ShowWindow=0. The command removes the .ps1 after running it.

The recovered PowerShell removes concatenation and substitutes H2O->quote, aWM->pipe and BIG->$ before IEX. It retrieves https://rough-truth-e072.publicftpresend.workers.dev/agygtsqurq, replaces * with A, reverses the string, Base64-decodes and passes the bytes to Reflection.Assembly.Load. It locates Mesa and invokes it with 19 encrypted configuration arguments.

CIL Mesa (method 0x46, RVA 0x13a84) forwards its arguments to DescriptografarEntradas. X4K7UjRa0C uses AES-CBC/PKCS7: the first 16 decoded bytes are the IV; the 32-byte key is UTF-8 password 006#5o6&qr1V padded with ascending byte values. Decryption exposes https://imperiailmports.com/img_000830.png, a Public Downloads destination, and MSBuild configuration. Configured MSBuild text alone is not claimed as observed process injection.

The current .png URL returns a 2,147,279-byte JPEG. Loader method tlYXicSJx carves INICIO/FIM markers, substitutes ###->A, reverses and Base64-decodes. This recovers a 34,816-byte .NET MALEY assembly.

Final assembly Main decrypts settings, establishes a mutex, copies its current image to %AppData%/windows.exe and creates a Startup windows.lnk using WScript.Shell. ConnectServer connects a TCP socket, sends Info and starts asynchronous reads. BeginReceive feeds complete frames to Messages.Read, which decrypts/splits operator commands. RunShell executes the supplied command; LN downloads and executes a supplied URL; FM and plugin commands load supplied code. Shutdown/restart and HTTP DoS tasking are also implemented.

Final configuration decryption uses AES-ECB with an MD5-derived overlapping-copy key. Recovered host is 31.56.209.61:443, group XWorm V7.1, separator <Xwormmm>. Static behavior plus configuration and an existing independent XWorm command-set detection support XWorm identification. Current live payloads are supplemental evidence and could differ from those originally served; the supplied HTA already proves concealed remote-code execution.
samples.source_label_explanation: The source label is consistent with directly proven concealed remote-code execution and the current XWorm delivery chain.

samples.identification: Sleipnir 3.23.0.0 Windows performance utility, PS2EXE packaged
samples.reason: Likely benign performance-tuning software: its extensive visible UI, user-triggered dispatch, backups/revert/history and vendor-verified update path explain its sensitive capabilities. Self-signing does not establish trust, and Defender exclusions/system hardening reductions remain accurate analyst findings. No supplied deployment context establishes abuse.
trace: Assembly Sleipnir 3.23.0.0 uses a conventional PS2EXE host. Entry method 0x72, RVA 0x455c reads the embedded Sleipnir.ps1 resource and passes it to a System.Management.Automation PowerShell runspace. Wrapper credential prompts, ReadKey dialogs and color/progress proxies are generic host support, not credential theft or keylogging.

The extracted 5,710-line script implements a visible WPF performance application. UI event handlers invoke tweak/profile dispatchers; dispatchers collect state, write backups, apply changes, verify and record local history. Individual changes include service/registry/network/power/game settings. Gaming profiles add Defender game-path/process exclusions and kill named background applications. These dangerous dual-use actions remain detected.

Its security-reducing changes include HVCI/VBS/hypervisor/CPU-mitigation settings and Defender scan limits/exclusions. Run/Startup paths are enumerated to disable existing startup applications through StartupApproved; no hidden self-installation is present. The foreground-window hook and hotkey implement Game Focus Lock; they do not record keystrokes or send data.

GPU update buttons open vendor pages. The optional NVIDIA/Intel silent-install path downloads a configured HTTPS URL, checks Authenticode Valid plus the expected publisher, requires a restore point, then starts the installer. Currently configured NVIDIA/Intel URLs return vendor support HTML, so executable-signature checks fail closed. The self-elevation fetch/IEX alternative has a REPLACE-WITH placeholder and is gated out for this requireAdministrator EXE.

osslsigncode independently confirms the PE Authenticode digest matches and the timestamp verifies, but the publisher CN=Sleipnir Local Publisher is self-signed; it is not a publicly trusted vendor signature. No substituted or appended executable was found. The single managed resource is the reviewed script.

Forager fetched NVIDIA and Intel support pages. The AMD URL redirects to an AMD Download-Incomplete page and fetch fails with HTTP/2 INTERNAL_ERROR after retries; no AMD installer was recovered. The code opens this AMD URL in a browser, and no hostile dependency destination was found.
samples.source_label_explanation: Possible heuristic/riskware reasons include PS2EXE embedding, self-signing, admin requirements, policy-bypass command text, Defender exclusions and security-reducing performance options. The exact reason for external engine labels is unknown.
samples.missing_context: No victim-machine execution history, user authorization record or deployment provenance is supplied. BENIGN is a sighted-quarantine decision, not ground-truth certification.
samples.marker_line: Sleipnir 3.23: UI-driven tuning; retain Defender exclusions

samples.identification: Atom's Connections 1.7.1.0 encrypted peer messaging desktop application
samples.reason: Likely benign encrypted messaging application: loopback-only native operations, bounded writes, own-key DPAPI and own-instance management match the advertised purpose; decoded web code and a verified dependency expose no malicious behavior. Obfuscation and unsigned packaging remain real facts. No supplied deployment context establishes abuse.
trace: Assembly AtomsConnections 1.7.1.0 by declared publisher Ultra Encode, LLC is unsigned. Main->Run hosts a desktop messaging application on http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ and http://localhost:<port>/. The default port is 47800. It registers an atoms: URL protocol and a desktop shortcut, not a login autorun.

LoadFiles reads app.pak, verifies its SHA-256 db2fd6b4dc620bdddf8cad94e451514066e9cd8181f40ba9a4905159800ccc3c and GZip-decompresses length-prefixed named records: index.html (616829 bytes), player.html (5019 bytes), vendor/peerjs.min.js (92865 bytes). Compressed resources explain the high executable entropy; this is not a native executable unpacker.

Run generates its own random 32-byte device.key and uses user-scope DPAPI Protect/Unprotect for that key. Handle validates Host and rejects cross-site state-changing calls. /device-key and /save require POST and X-Atoms:1. /save only writes beneath application picture/document roots; SafeTarget rejects traversal, separators, reserved device names and paths outside the chosen root.

EndOtherCopies queries processes with its own executable basename, excludes itself and requires the same configured port before Kill. This serves single-instance recovery, not security-product termination. The local listener does not dispatch remote OS commands.

Pure-decoder extraction decoded 10,979 obfuscated calls without running the app. The JavaScript implements encrypted local storage/device binding, PeerJS encrypted peer messaging, user-initiated media/calls, save/export UI, version checks, and opt-in plugins. Its JavaScript-obfuscator rotation/base64 string-array machinery is real; both extracted HTML resources retain their suspicious obfuscation findings.

PeerJS broker is 0.peerjs.com:443 with peerjs key. The bundled library matches npm peerjs@1.5.4 package/dist/peerjs.min.js byte for byte (SHA-256 ad5d8870d1e389914f9cba8d35be313c4327c69ee0a221e482e9bf7621136fe5). No modified dependency was found.

Forager recovered atomsconnections.com, version.json and plugins/catalog.json. Both catalogued archives match their advertised SHA-256: Neon Arcade 1.7.0 and Atom Math Lab 1.4.0. Their manifests and contents implement games; standalone recursive scans found no hostile or suspicious findings. Optional plugin content is rendered in allow-scripts iframes without allow-same-origin, with connect-src none, and messages/permissions are mediated by the parent app. Current web content may differ from the historical 1.7.1 artifact.
samples.source_label_explanation: Possible heuristic reasons include high-entropy compressed resources, deliberately obfuscated HTML/JavaScript, a local HTTP server, DPAPI, registry writes and process-management code. The exact reason for external engine labels is unknown.
samples.missing_context: No victim-machine execution history, user authorization record or deployment provenance is supplied. BENIGN is a sighted-quarantine decision, not ground-truth certification.
samples.marker_line: Atom's Connections 1.7.1: encrypted messaging; no abuse found

rule_changes.new_neutral_binding: micro-behaviors/process/deploy/script-eval::html-response-text-binding-eval uses HTML-scoped inline YARA to compare the stored response variable and eval argument byte for byte, prohibit intervening reassignment, constrain the same script element and permit restricted nonmutating guards. It supplies an actual source-to-sink link instead of separate tokens. Existing standalone JavaScript AST matching is unchanged.
rule_changes.migrated_and_corrected: Moved hta-offscreen-serverxmlhttp-response-eval from objectives/command-and-control/dropper/delivery/fetch-exec to objectives/execution/payload/script-eval. Payload evaluation is execution rather than an operator-control channel. Replaced unbound responseText/eval legs with the neutral binding; preserved HTA, offscreen, ActiveX, ServerXMLHTTP and synchronous-GET requirements. Other five rules in the source file remain unchanged.
rule_changes.new_evasion: objectives/evasion/process/hidden/execution::hta-conceals-response-evaluation requires HTA markup, hidden/minimized presentation, offscreen/trivial resize and the bound response evaluation. This describes concealment, separately from payload activation.
rule_changes.severity_correction: Removed the execution-policy-bypass composite downgrade for RunAs or Expand-Archive. Policy-bypass options remain notable even during elevation or archive work; they are not nearly universal baseline behavior. All matching and all original findings are preserved.
rule_changes.consumer_audit: No exact consumers of the old HTA ID. Two relevant ancestor selectors were inspected: crystalx-rat excludes command-and-control under PE-only 5-15MB scope; windows-embedded-security-hosts-sinkhole selects dropper under PE/DLL scope. The migrated HTML-only observation cannot have affected either file-scoped consumer. Their YAML and effective coverage remain unchanged. The neutral target deploy/script-eval has no broad ancestor-selector consumer that would inherit this new atom.
rule_changes.coverage_losses: No original sample lost any finding. In controlled old-rule scans, mismatched variables, overwritten responses, prefix names, a member evaluator, a property binding and separate script elements falsely inherited hostile response-execution claims. The corrected rule rejects these; these are intentional false-positive corrections, not suppressed true attack chains. Retained adjacent, renamed and guarded attacks pass.
rule_changes.placement: Neutral acquired-response-to-evaluator relation -> process/deploy/script-eval; admitted offscreen privileged HTA chain -> execution/payload/script-eval; suppression of the evaluation window -> evasion/process/hidden/execution. No taxonomy branch or classifier weighting was invented.

remaining_gaps: The original UTF-16 HTA is classified unknown by the current engine and receives zero YAML findings before and after; YAML for: unknown is explicitly unsupported. UTF-8 analysis copies route to HTML and show both hostile objectives. This leaves the original malicious sample below the minimum firing-trait coverage despite strong manual proof. Do not add invalid unknown rules or pretend normalization fixed the original artifact.

All three original samples have calibrated ML level -1 before/after. For the malicious original HTA this is a classifier miss (probability 0.000019321838 unchanged). The normalized HTA retains its original attack detection, now correctly placed and bound, and gains a separate concealment finding; ML probability rises from 0.98899895 to 0.9938969 but remains calibrated level -1. Hostile rule findings are present independently of the ML grid.

The engine does not recursively expose these custom managed resources as archive members. Atom app.pak, its HTML, vendor library and optional fetched plugin archives were manually extracted/scanned. The extracted HTML obfuscation is correctly suspicious even though the application verdict is BENIGN. The original PE has no such resource-level findings; no inaccurate generic entropy-to-obfuscation inference was added.

Fetched URLs reflect live 2026-10-22 content, not immutable historical payloads. No runtime success, victim installation or deployment authorization is inferred. AMD installer recovery failed after the vendor redirected it to a download-error page.
Atomscan reports its bundled model feature specification as v18 while the extractor is v19; scan warnings describe forward-compatible zero filling. Classifier results are reported as observed.

verification.focused_cases: 16 expected rule-set cases pass; see cases.json, results.json and check.py. Four existing hostile guarded JavaScript fixtures and two benign rebound/other-variable fixtures have exactly identical complete finding maps before and after.
verification.original_rescans: All three originals were rescanned after final YAML changes, with no detection losses; the only criticality change is policy-bypass baseline->notable. No original is an archive, and each original produces one analysis unit.
verification.normalized_rescan: One old hostile HTA objective retained under its correct ID/path with stronger binding; one new hostile concealment objective. No duplicate payload objective remains.
verification.validation_command: make validate (the final action after report and marker creation)
